trials.claim: Manage scheduled and draft posts from calendar widget with full editorial calendar view
trials.claimQuote: Easily manage your scheduled and draft posts right from the stunning calendar (thanks to the tool’s widget) and get a full view of your content in the editorial calendar.
trials.reasoning: A buyer reports manual scheduling does not work and support had not resolved it, which directly undercuts managing scheduled posts from the calendar despite the vendor's calendar description.

exhibits.quote: Manual scheduling does not work! Raised to support, still waiting on their feedback.
exhibits.argument: Manual scheduling from the calendar is reported as non-functional, undermining calendar management.

exhibits.quote: With SchedulePress, you’ll have a bird’s eye view of your posting schedule via Editorial Calendar & Dashboard Widget.
exhibits.argument: The quote confirms both an editorial calendar and dashboard widget provide a full view of the posting schedule.

exhibits.quote: The calendar is easy to use, and like that drafts are separated.
exhibits.argument: The buyer confirms the calendar manages posts while keeping drafts separated as claimed.

trials.claim: Schedule WordPress posts in advance and manage all authors in one place
trials.claimQuote: Schedule your WordPress posts in advance and manage all authors in one place.
trials.reasoning: Buyers report scheduled posts failing to publish and the product not working with Editor or Author roles, contradicting both reliable advance scheduling and managing all authors in one place.

exhibits.quote: Scheduled 3 posts and only one was published. The other two are stuck in scheduled status even though the scheduled publish date has passed.
exhibits.argument: Scheduled posts failed to publish on time, contradicting reliable advance scheduling.

exhibits.quote: My biggest issue with the product is that it doesn't work with Editor or Author roles.
exhibits.argument: Lack of Editor and Author role support undermines managing all authors in one place.

exhibits.quote: As your one-stop shop for planning, creating, and scheduling blog posts on your WordPress site, SchedulePress makes it easy to stay on top of your content strategy and your content team.
exhibits.argument: The vendor describes the product as a one-stop shop for scheduling WordPress posts and managing the content team.

exhibits.quote: This plugin helps ensure I have my content scheduled days in advance and I look at it daily on my dashboard.
exhibits.argument: A customer testimonial confirms the plugin schedules content days in advance and is monitored daily from the dashboard.

trials.claim: Create, edit and move posts with drag-and-drop feature
trials.claimQuote: Create, edit, and move posts easily with the intuitive drag-and-drop feature.
trials.reasoning: A buyer reports edits in the scheduler are deleted after leaving the screen despite a saved message, which directly undercuts the claimed create-and-edit drag-and-drop workflow.

exhibits.quote: After some experimenting, I see that although I set the schedule, hit save, get a saved message, It deletes all my work after I leave the screen.
exhibits.argument: Edits made in the scheduler are deleted after leaving, contradicting reliable edit functionality.

exhibits.quote: Manage your content with a great visual calendar. Supports drag and drop organization and you can create new posts right from the calendar.
exhibits.argument: The vendor states the calendar supports drag-and-drop organization and creating new posts directly from it.

exhibits.quote: includes a calendar view that lets you drag posts around and shows any unscheduled drafts.
exhibits.argument: The vendor testimonial confirms users can move posts by dragging them around in the calendar view.
